notes: Brackets apply to Connecticut taxable income (Tax Calculation Schedule Line 3 = Connecticut AGI minus the Table A exemption). Table B prints one schedule for Single or Married Filing Separately, one for Married Filing Jointly/Qualifying Surviving Spouse and one for Head of Household, so married_separate is not given (it uses single) and qualifying surviving spouse uses married_joint.

Final tax is not the Table B arithmetic alone: Line 7 = Table B tax + Table C 2% add-back + Table D recapture, then less Line 7 x the Table E decimal (Lines 8-10). Tables C and D are in recapture (their step amounts in as_printed, which the format holds only as text); Table E is the personal_tax_credit relief.

Line 6: tax is 0 if Connecticut AGI is 12,000 or less (MFS), 15,000 or less (single), 19,000 or less (HOH), 24,000 or less (MFJ or QSS). Tax Tables on the DRS website may be used when Connecticut AGI is 102,000 or less (not in the sources); the Tax Calculation Schedule is used above that.
The booklet prints no standard deduction, no dependent exemption and no age-65 or blindness amount; the only exemption is the Table A personal exemption by filing status.

Social Security: treatment 'relief'. Fully subtracted (the federally taxable amount) when federal AGI is under 75,000 (single, MFS) or 100,000 (MFJ, QSS, HOH); at or above, the worksheet subtracts taxable benefits less 25% of the lesser of worksheet Lines A and B. No upper income limit is printed. Checked on PDF page 8 (Line 41), page 24 (worksheet) and the form's Line 41.
Roth conversions: the booklet excludes 'Distributions from Roth IRAs' but does not say whether taxable conversions count; roth_conversion is in covers_unclear for both Line 48b entries.

Pensions from other states' governments (brief rule 15a): the booklet does not name them; the Line 48b worksheet (PDF page 24, Line 2) takes 100% of federal Line 5b less only military retirement pay, Tier 1 and Tier 2 railroad retirement and Connecticut teachers' pay, so they are in the same entry as Connecticut and federal pensions (public_pension_other_state in covers). No reciprocity rule is printed.

Capital gains: no rate or deduction different from ordinary income found in the booklet. Surtaxes: none printed (Tables C and D are the high-income mechanism). Indexing: the booklet says nothing about inflation adjustment for any figure.

Not recorded: Schedule 1 Line 42 (state and local income tax refunds) and the other Line 46-49 modifications (fiduciary, bonds, tribal members, organ donation up to 10,000, and similar), credit for taxes paid to qualifying jurisdictions (Schedule 2), Schedule CT-IT credits, claim of right, CT AMT and use tax.
Shares of the covered income: the 50% teachers' subtraction and the 75% IRA share are each entry's share (0.5, 0.75); the Line 48b phase-out decimals multiply the IRA's 75% (worksheet Line 2).

Property tax credit steps: keep_share is 1 minus the printed decimal (.15 -> .85, .30 -> .70, .45 -> .55, .60 -> .40, .75 -> .25, .90 -> .10, 1.00 -> 0), because the printed decimal is the share removed (Line 67 = Line 65 x Line 66).

Pension and IRA steps: the Phase-Out Table bands are 'greater than or equal to' / 'less than or equal to' whole dollars, so a step's 'over' is the printed upper end of the band below (over 74,999 means 75,000 or more). Table A, C, D, E and property tax bands are 'More Than' / 'Less Than or Equal To' and their 'over' is the printed 'More Than' figure.
